raw_response:
I have worked this land since I was a young man. My father farmed here in Quzhou, and his father before him. The land is flat, the water table is reachable — I know what this ground wants.

I have 12 mu. Same as last year. Same as the year before.

I will plant winter wheat on all 12 mu in October, after the summer corn comes off. That is what I do. That is what everyone here does. The wheat-corn rotation is how we feed ourselves and pay for everything. I will not change it. Some younger men in the village tried vegetables last year, but vegetable prices crashed in May and they lost money. I stick to grain.

For wheat I will buy improved seed from the township cooperative — probably Jimai 22 or similar, whatever they stock. Hybrid wheat is not common here and I don't trust it. I will do base fertilizer before planting — compound fertilizer with nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium — and then top-dress with urea at the jointing stage when the crop needs it most. I irrigate four times: pre-sowing to wet the seedbed, once in winter if it's dry, at jointing, and at heading. I spray twice — spring disease pressure here is always powdery mildew and rust, and then aphids before harvest. I'll use the rotary tiller to work in the maize stalks before planting.

For summer maize I plant right after wheat harvest in June, no delay. I use hybrid seed — Xianyu 335 if I can get it, Zhengdan 958 if not. These always yield well for me. I rotary till quickly and get the seed in within a week of wheat harvest. Summer rains usually help but I will irrigate twice to be safe — once at tasseling, once at grain fill if it's hot and dry. I spray twice: once early for corn borer, once if I see blight spreading.

I expect maybe 450 jin per mu for wheat, around 560 jin per mu for corn. Not a record year, just a stable year. That is all I want.
